Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11 - Minor: the run settings label the current period q2-2027 and the prior period fy-2026, but the filings show the third quarter of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025. The filings control every period label in this run; the settings labels were not used as evidence. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 1 - Minor: the interim reports do not repeat the debt table by note and give principal only as a rounded total, so principal by note after the second-quarter repurchases is not stated in any supplied file. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 26 - Minor: governance detail (board, ownership, compensation) is incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the guarantor list is filed as an exhibit that was not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 109 - Minor: the annual report cover dates the share count February 9, 2025, which falls before the fiscal year it reports; this is probably a typing error and the share count is not used. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 2 - Minor: the file names carry period-end dates, while the filing dates stated in the documents are later; the document dates in the source list are the filing or signature dates stated inside each file. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 28

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Reported EBITDA, calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortisation, was USD 508 million for the twelve months to 2026-10-10 against USD 200 million of cash interest, a cover of 2.54x. About USD 2,300 million of the cash sits in accounts under springing control agreements, and the only committed backstop is USD 894 million of undrawn asset-based facility. The next maturity is USD 350 million of notes due in October 2027. No credit agreement, indenture or rating was supplied, so covenant headroom is not established. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Gross leverage is the weak point of the credit, and it improved only because earnings recovered. Total debt of USD 3,388 million is 6.67x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, against 14.90x at the 2025 year end, when reported EBITDA was USD 229 million after USD 204 million of restructuring and related expenses. For 2024 the ratio is not calculable because reported EBITDA was USD -421 million. Debt rose because the company issued USD 1,950 million of senior unsecured notes in August 2025 and repaid USD 300 million of 2026 notes, and it kept the rest as cash, so net debt is USD 303 million, or 0.60x. Bondholders are therefore exposed to how that cash is used: it is both the cushion and the reason net leverage looks low. Basis: calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C15; calculation C01; calculation C02; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 66–68, 86–87

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Interest cover is adequate on cash interest and weaker on interest actually accrued. Last-twelve-month reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 200 million 2.54x and interest expense of USD 213 million 2.38x. Cash interest understated the burden in 2025: USD 76 million was paid against USD 139 million of expense, because the first coupons on the new notes fell in 2026 and accrued interest rose from USD 23 million to USD 79 million. The last twelve months carry two coupons on the new notes, and the contractual annual coupon on year-end principal is USD 195.88 million, so USD 200 million is a fair run-rate. Other income, net of USD 106 million over the last twelve months, which the company attributes mainly to interest on invested cash, offsets part of the cost. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash generation has turned, driven by payables as much as by earnings. Operating cash flow was USD 311 million in the forty weeks to 2026-10-10 against USD -118 million a year earlier, and after USD 202 million of capital expenditure free cash flow was USD 109 million against USD -277 million. Accounts payable moved from a USD 270 million outflow to a USD 94 million inflow, and fiscal 2025 operating cash flow of USD -46 million reflected a USD 469 million payables outflow. Payables are largely supplier-financed: confirmed obligations were USD 2,600 million against accounts payable of USD 3,065 million. These obligations sit outside debt, but a withdrawal by the participating banks, which the annual report links to the company's credit rating, would shorten payment terms and consume cash, so this float is the main swing factor in liquidity. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is USD 3,979 million, made of USD 3,085 million of cash and USD 894 million of undrawn asset-based facility after USD 106 million of letters of credit. About USD 2,300 million of the cash is designated qualified cash in accounts that become restricted on a default or covenant breach, and the facility requires minimum availability of the greater of 12.5% of the line cap and USD 125 million and excess availability of at least USD 400 million. facts.text: Three definitions drive the numbers. Reported EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortisation, which leaves out other income, net and so excludes interest income. The company's adjusted EBITDAR of USD 1,157 million also adds back rent expense of USD 524 million, share-based compensation of USD 37 million and USD 89 million of transformation and other charges, so it is not comparable with USD 508 million, and the 2.2x ratio built on it adds lease liabilities of USD 2,189 million to debt. The company also deducts all cash although about USD 2,300 million is under springing control. Periods differ: fiscal 2025 has fifty-three weeks, the interim periods are forty weeks and are labelled nine months in the tables, and the last twelve months span fifty-three weeks. facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is operating recovery. Forty-week reported EBITDA was USD 406 million against USD 127 million, operating income was USD 218 million against USD -87 million, restructuring expense fell from USD 180 million to USD 84 million, gross margin rose to 45.29% from 43.21%, and free cash flow was USD 109 million, with guidance raised to about USD 150 million for fiscal 2026. The company's own net leverage has been 2.4x, 2.1x and 2.2x across the three quarters of 2026. This view would win if earnings keep rising while the cash is held and the maturities to 2030 are met from cash. The view would turn weaker if confirmed supplier-finance obligations fall sharply from USD 2,600 million, or if cash is used in a way that lifts net debt well above USD 303 million without a matching rise in EBITDA. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 12 - Low: lines printed as a dash in the statements are not read as zero: other investing, net in 2024 and the nine months of 2025; discontinued investing in 2025 and the nine months of 2025; proceeds from issuance of long-term debt, repayment of long-term debt and debt issuance costs in 2024 and the nine months of 2026 where printed as dashes; and the current portion of long-term debt at the 2025 and 2024 year ends. They restrict only the tied lines and the totals still add. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 68, 87; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 6 - Low: interest income is inside other income, net and not printed separately, interim cash taxes paid, the maintenance and growth split of capital expenditure, acquisitions, the discontinued-operations line of the interim income statements, share repurchases as a cash line and the ABL rate floor and maturity date are not printed in the supplied files, so none is used. Closing them needs the full agreements or a fuller cash flow note. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 68, 90, 105; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 15–16 - Low: no pension or retiree medical obligation is disclosed, comparable store sales and the Carquest store count for 2024 and the nine months of 2025 were not read, and the issuer reconciles adjusted operating income and its margin only for the forty-week periods, so those cells are not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 47; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10 - Low: Source readiness notes that the run settings label the current period q2-2027, which conflicts with the filings; no figure here uses that label, and fiscal 2025 has fifty-three weeks while the interim periods are forty weeks labelled nine months. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 69

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: The business is a single segment, about half professional trade customers and half do-it-yourself, concentrated in the United States, and in the second year of a restructuring that closed 10.90% of its stores and followed the sale of Worldpac for net proceeds of USD 1,440 million. Net sales fell 5.4% in fiscal 2025 on the closures. Governance evidence is thin: the proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition and large holders are not established, and a securities class action dismissed in 2025 is on appeal. The sponsor and governance risk level is Medium because the evidence is mixed rather than adverse. Basis: calculation C04; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 39, 100, 105; Source readiness (CP-0)

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: No sponsor stands behind this credit, and governance evidence is incomplete. The common stock is listed and widely held, the annual report names no controlling holder, and the items on directors, ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied, so board composition, large holders, related-party dealings and any fees are not established. The consequence is that there is no evidenced route for equity support or for sponsor extraction, and creditor protection rests on documents that were not supplied rather than on an owner's willingness. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 37, 61; Source readiness (CP-0)

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder payouts are modest and have been cut, but they were paid while free cash flow was negative. Dividends declared per share fell from USD 2.25 in fiscal 2023 to USD 1.00 in fiscal 2024 and 2025, and no shares were bought back under the programme in either of those years. Even so, the company paid USD 60 million of dividends in fiscal 2025 when operating cash flow was USD -46 million and free cash flow was USD -298 million, so cash consumed after dividends was USD -358 million, which cash balances enlarged by the August 2025 note issue absorbed. The mechanism is a small distribution funded in effect by new debt; the size is minor against the cash balance, but the ABL restrictions on larger payouts are known only from the company's summary. Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 52, 67–68, 101; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The August 2025 refinancing pre-funded maturities but moved the revolver from unsecured to secured. The company issued USD 1,950 million of senior unsecured notes, redeemed USD 300 million of 2026 notes and replaced an unsecured USD 1,000 million revolver with a first-lien asset-based facility over receivables, inventory and cash. The facility is undrawn, but a drawing would rank ahead of the notes in those assets, and about three quarters of the cash sits in accounts under springing control that become restricted on a default or covenant breach. Noteholders therefore gained maturity cover and lost priority on the most liquid assets. Basis: calculation C05; calculation C11; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 87–92, 105; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 12

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The operating model is mid-recovery and depends on supplier finance. Net sales were USD 8,601 million in fiscal 2025, down 5.4% on closures partly offset by the fifty-third week, with comparable store sales up 0.8%. Professional customers are about half of sales, nearly all sales are in the United States, and about 80% of stores are leased, so rent is a large fixed claim. Confirmed supplier finance obligations of USD 2,600 million fund most of accounts payable, and the annual report ties bank participation to the company's credit rating, so a downgrade could shorten payment terms and consume cash. facts.text: Controls and litigation are mixed rather than adverse. Internal control over financial reporting was effective at the 2025 year end after material weaknesses disclosed earlier, and the company still booked a small remediation cost in fiscal 2025. facts.text: The strongest evidence for a better view is financial discipline and recovery: the dividend was cut by more than half in 2024, the company holds USD 3,085 million of cash against USD 3,388 million of debt, comparable store sales turned positive in the last four weeks of the third quarter, and the company has raised its fiscal 2026 free cash flow guidance to about USD 150 million. The view would improve if the proxy statement showed no large holder or related-party arrangement and the credit documents showed tight restricted-payment limits. It would worsen if the credit documents allowed large payouts, if confirmed supplier finance obligations fell sharply from USD 2,600 million, or if the appeal revived the securities class action with a quantified claim. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against caution is that net debt is small and the company's own net leverage is 2.2x, down from 2.4x two quarters earlier, with free cash flow guidance raised to about USD 150 million and comparable sales turning positive in the last four weeks of the third quarter. If the recovery holds, reported EBITDA above the last-twelve-month USD 508 million would move leverage below 6.67x without any debt repayment. The case for more caution is that the cash reflects the Worldpac proceeds and the 2025 notes rather than operating cash generation, USD 2,300 million of it is under springing control, and USD 2,600 million of supplier finance is rating-linked. The view would improve with sustained earnings growth and a rating that supports the supplier programs; it would worsen if confirmed supplier finance obligations fall sharply, if cash is used for payouts or deals, or if availability under the facility shrinks toward its stated floors. facts.text: The strongest credit support is liquidity: USD 3,979 million of cash and availability against USD 650 million of notes due in 2027 and 2028 removes near-term refinancing pressure and gives time for the turnaround. A fifth is the maturity profile, which is entirely fixed-rate unsecured notes with no scheduled maturity until October 2027. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: The company is a North American aftermarket auto parts retailer and distributor serving professional installers and do-it-yourself customers from company stores, independently owned Carquest stores and online, with net sales of USD 8,601 million in fiscal 2025 and nearly all of them in the United States. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most: the company competes with national chains, independents, internet retailers and dealers on availability, price and service, and the filing warns that the company might not be able to pass higher supplier costs on to customers, so pricing power is limited and gross margin depends on mix and sourcing. Supplier power is the next, because the company buys from several hundred vendors and relies on favourable payment terms and supplier finance, which a downgrade could remove. In the analyst's judgement buyer power is moderate for professionals, who value same-day availability, and higher for do-it-yourself customers, who can switch easily. The threat of new entrants and substitutes is mainly online retail and changes in vehicle use, which are slow-moving credit risks rather than near-term ones. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a withdrawal by banks from the supplier finance programs, for example after a rating action, at a time when comparable sales are again negative. The first operational break is shorter payment terms on inventory, which in fiscal 2025 produced a USD 469 million payables outflow that contributed to operating cash flow of USD -46 million even without a bank withdrawal. The financial transmission is cash falling, free cash flow turning negative as capex of about USD 300 million continues, and EBITDA falling back to the fiscal 2025 level of USD 229 million, which would put total debt of USD 3,388 million at 14.79x and cover cash interest of USD 200 million only 1.15x. Cash and availability of USD 3,979 million would cover the 2027 and 2028 notes in that case, but they would not cover the 2030 wall, and restricted cash and availability floors would reduce usable liquidity. Management levers are cutting capex, slowing store openings and withholding dividends; the observable triggers are falling confirmed supplier finance, negative comparable sales and shrinking facility availability. Basis: calculation C03; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C18; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 49, 67–68

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and earnings releases are enough to build a financial and business snapshot of Advance Auto Parts through the quarter ended October 10, 2026, but not enough to assess legal priority, covenant capacity or market-implied risk.

The annual report gives audited statements, the note-by-note debt table and the maturity ladder; the three quarterly reports and three earnings releases add interim balance sheets, liquidity and the company's own leverage reconciliation. No credit agreement, indenture, rating, market price, peer set or portfolio limit was supplied, so creditor protections rest on the company's own summaries of those documents. The run settings label the current period as the second quarter of 2027, which conflicts with the filings; the filings control.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors rest on cash rather than earnings: net debt is only USD 303 million, but total debt is 6.67x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, so the credit depends on the USD 3,085 million cash balance staying accessible.

Reported EBITDA, calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortisation, was USD 508 million for the twelve months to 2026-10-10 against USD 200 million of cash interest, a cover of 2.54x. The company's own adjusted measure, which also adds back rent, shows 2.2x and is a different perimeter. About USD 2,300 million of the cash sits in accounts under springing control agreements, and the only committed backstop is USD 894 million of undrawn asset-based facility. The next maturity is USD 350 million of notes due in October 2027. No credit agreement, indenture or rating was supplied, so covenant headroom is not established.

Basis: calculation C14; calculation C19; calculation C05; calculation C07; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 89, 92
### Key findings

Gross leverage is the weak point of the credit, and it improved only because earnings recovered. Total debt of USD 3,388 million is 6.67x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, against 14.90x at the 2025 year end, when reported EBITDA was USD 229 million after USD 204 million of restructuring and related expenses. For 2024 the ratio is not calculable because reported EBITDA was USD -421 million. Debt rose because the company issued USD 1,950 million of senior unsecured notes in August 2025 and repaid USD 300 million of 2026 notes, and it kept the rest as cash, so net debt is USD 303 million, or 0.60x. Bondholders are therefore exposed to how that cash is used: it is both the cushion and the reason net leverage looks low.
Basis: calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C15; calculation C01; calculation C02; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 66–68, 86–87

Interest cover is adequate on cash interest and weaker on interest actually accrued. Last-twelve-month reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 200 million 2.54x and interest expense of USD 213 million 2.38x. Cash interest understated the burden in 2025: USD 76 million was paid against USD 139 million of expense, because the first coupons on the new notes fell in 2026 and accrued interest rose from USD 23 million to USD 79 million. The last twelve months carry two coupons on the new notes, and the contractual annual coupon on year-end principal is USD 195.88 million, so USD 200 million is a fair run-rate. Other income, net of USD 106 million over the last twelve months, which the company attributes mainly to interest on invested cash, offsets part of the cost.

Basis: calculation C07; calculation C09; calculation C21; calculation C37; calculation C33; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 68, 87, 94; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7, 24

Cash generation has turned, driven by payables as much as by earnings. Operating cash flow was USD 311 million in the forty weeks to 2026-10-10 against USD -118 million a year earlier, and after USD 202 million of capital expenditure free cash flow was USD 109 million against USD -277 million. Accounts payable moved from a USD 270 million outflow to a USD 94 million inflow, and fiscal 2025 operating cash flow of USD -46 million reflected a USD 469 million payables outflow. Payables are largely supplier-financed: confirmed obligations were USD 2,600 million against accounts payable of USD 3,065 million. These obligations sit outside debt, but a withdrawal by the participating banks, which the annual report links to the company's credit rating, would shorten payment terms and consume cash, so this float is the main swing factor in liquidity.

Liquidity is USD 3,979 million, made of USD 3,085 million of cash and USD 894 million of undrawn asset-based facility after USD 106 million of letters of credit. About USD 2,300 million of the cash is designated qualified cash in accounts that become restricted on a default or covenant breach, and the facility requires minimum availability of the greater of 12.5% of the line cap and USD 125 million and excess availability of at least USD 400 million. The company reports compliance, but headroom is not established without the credit agreement. The next maturities are the 2027 notes of USD 350 million and the 2028 notes of USD 300 million at year-end principal, both within reach of cash.
Basis: calculation C29; calculation C30; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 89–92

Funded debt is entirely senior unsecured notes: USD 3,450 million of principal at the 2025 year end in six series, with USD 350 million due in FY2027, USD 300 million in FY2028, USD 1,475 million in FY2030 and USD 1,325 million in FY2032 and FY2033. The undrawn USD 1,000 million first-lien asset-based facility ranks ahead of the notes against receivables, inventory and cash, so a drawing would be senior to the notes in those assets; the subsidiary guarantor list was not supplied, so structural priority beyond that is not established. Claims outside debt are large: operating lease liabilities of USD 2,189 million, USD 549 million of cash paid on operating leases in fiscal 2025, supplier finance of USD 2,600 million, USD 57 million of guaranteed bank loans to independent stores, and a final USD 55 million Worldpac working-capital payment made in 2026.

Basis: calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 86–91, 94, 106; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 12–14; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 10

Three definitions drive the numbers. Reported EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortisation, which leaves out other income, net and so excludes interest income. The company's adjusted EBITDAR of USD 1,157 million also adds back rent expense of USD 524 million, share-based compensation of USD 37 million and USD 89 million of transformation and other charges, so it is not comparable with USD 508 million, and the 2.2x ratio built on it adds lease liabilities of USD 2,189 million to debt. The company also deducts all cash although about USD 2,300 million is under springing control. Periods differ: fiscal 2025 has fifty-three weeks, the interim periods are forty weeks and are labelled nine months in the tables, and the last twelve months span fifty-three weeks.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C38; calculation C39; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 69
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is operating recovery. Forty-week reported EBITDA was USD 406 million against USD 127 million, operating income was USD 218 million against USD -87 million, restructuring expense fell from USD 180 million to USD 84 million, gross margin rose to 45.29% from 43.21%, and free cash flow was USD 109 million, with guidance raised to about USD 150 million for fiscal 2026. The company's own net leverage has been 2.4x, 2.1x and 2.2x across the three quarters of 2026. This view would win if earnings keep rising while the cash is held and the maturities to 2030 are met from cash. The view would turn weaker if confirmed supplier-finance obligations fall sharply from USD 2,600 million, or if cash is used in a way that lifts net debt well above USD 303 million without a matching rise in EBITDA.

Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C35; EX-99.1_2026-05-21_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-08-20_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-04-25_aap-20260425.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-18_aap-20260718.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Limitations

No credit agreement, indenture, rating, market price or peer set was supplied, so covenant headroom, guarantor coverage and relative value are not established. Principal by note after the 2026 repurchases is not stated in the quarterly reports, so the maturity ladder, debt stack and debt reconciliation are drawn at the 2025 year end. Adjusted EBITDA is not stated by the company, which reports adjusted EBITDAR, so no adjusted leverage or cover row is given. Cash interest is paid twice a year on most notes, so any single interim period is lumpy and only the last twelve months are used.

- High: the executed ABL credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied, so maintenance covenant levels beyond the company's own summary, covenant headroom and the guarantor group are not established; this restricts any statement on covenant capacity or structural priority. - Medium: the balance sheet at 2025-10-04 was not supplied because the third-quarter report for 2025 is not among the sources, so the nine-month 2025 column has flows but no balance sheet, and the 2025 store count and comparable sales are not established. Closing it needs that report.

- Medium: all cash is deducted in net debt although about USD 2,300 million is qualified cash under springing control agreements, so net debt may understate the debt the company can service from freely usable cash. Closing it needs the credit agreement terms on the control triggers.

Closing them needs the full agreements or a fuller cash flow note.

Business and governance fact base for ADVANCE AUTO PARTS INC as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the issuer's business, ownership, operating model, transactions, event history and governance and financial-policy behaviour, taken from the seven supplied filings and earnings releases.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Advance Auto Parts is a widely held retailer with no sponsor, so creditors depend on the company's own financial policy, which has cut shareholder payouts and pre-funded maturities but also placed a secured facility ahead of the unsecured notes.

The business is a single segment, about half professional trade customers and half do-it-yourself, concentrated in the United States, and in the second year of a restructuring that closed 10.90% of its stores and followed the sale of Worldpac for net proceeds of USD 1,440 million. Net sales fell 5.4% in fiscal 2025 on the closures. Governance evidence is thin: the proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition and large holders are not established, and a securities class action dismissed in 2025 is on appeal. The sponsor and governance risk level is Medium because the evidence is mixed rather than adverse.
Basis: calculation C04; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 39, 100, 105; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

No sponsor stands behind this credit, and governance evidence is incomplete. The common stock is listed and widely held, the annual report names no controlling holder, and the items on directors, ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied, so board composition, large holders, related-party dealings and any fees are not established. The consequence is that there is no evidenced route for equity support or for sponsor extraction, and creditor protection rests on documents that were not supplied rather than on an owner's willingness.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 37, 61; Source readiness (CP-0)

Shareholder payouts are modest and have been cut, but they were paid while free cash flow was negative. Dividends declared per share fell from USD 2.25 in fiscal 2023 to USD 1.00 in fiscal 2024 and 2025, and no shares were bought back under the programme in either of those years. Even so, the company paid USD 60 million of dividends in fiscal 2025 when operating cash flow was USD -46 million and free cash flow was USD -298 million, so cash consumed after dividends was USD -358 million, which cash balances enlarged by the August 2025 note issue absorbed. The mechanism is a small distribution funded in effect by new debt; the size is minor against the cash balance, but the ABL restrictions on larger payouts are known only from the company's summary.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 52, 67–68, 101; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

The August 2025 refinancing pre-funded maturities but moved the revolver from unsecured to secured. The company issued USD 1,950 million of senior unsecured notes, redeemed USD 300 million of 2026 notes and replaced an unsecured USD 1,000 million revolver with a first-lien asset-based facility over receivables, inventory and cash. The facility is undrawn, but a drawing would rank ahead of the notes in those assets, and about three quarters of the cash sits in accounts under springing control that become restricted on a default or covenant breach. Noteholders therefore gained maturity cover and lost priority on the most liquid assets.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C11; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 87–92, 105; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 12

The operating model is mid-recovery and depends on supplier finance. Net sales were USD 8,601 million in fiscal 2025, down 5.4% on closures partly offset by the fifty-third week, with comparable store sales up 0.8%. Professional customers are about half of sales, nearly all sales are in the United States, and about 80% of stores are leased, so rent is a large fixed claim. Confirmed supplier finance obligations of USD 2,600 million fund most of accounts payable, and the annual report ties bank participation to the company's credit rating, so a downgrade could shorten payment terms and consume cash.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C10; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 33, 39, 42, 49, 103, 105; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 14

Controls and litigation are mixed rather than adverse. Internal control over financial reporting was effective at the 2025 year end after material weaknesses disclosed earlier, and the company still booked a small remediation cost in fiscal 2025. A securities class action and related derivative suits remain open after the dismissal was appealed, and executive turnover costs were recorded in each of the last three years. These are monitoring points; none is quantified as a creditor claim in the filings.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is financial discipline and recovery: the dividend was cut by more than half in 2024, the company holds USD 3,085 million of cash against USD 3,388 million of debt, comparable store sales turned positive in the last four weeks of the third quarter, and the company has raised its fiscal 2026 free cash flow guidance to about USD 150 million. The view would improve if the proxy statement showed no large holder or related-party arrangement and the credit documents showed tight restricted-payment limits. It would worsen if the credit documents allowed large payouts, if confirmed supplier finance obligations fell sharply from USD 2,600 million, or if the appeal revived the securities class action with a quantified claim.
Basis: calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 14; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 103

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The company has no pending acquisition, buyout or sponsor transaction in the supplied files; its transactions are a disposal, a restructuring and a refinancing. It sold the Worldpac business, which closed on 2024-11-01 for net proceeds of about USD 1,440 million after costs against a headline price of USD 1,500 million, and the final working capital adjustment led to a USD 55 million payment in 2026. The 2024 Restructuring Plan, approved on 2024-11-13, closed the intended stores and independent locations in the first quarter of 2025 at a cumulative restructuring cost of USD 1,100 million across active plans.

New debt was issued on 2025-08-04: USD 975 million of notes due 2030 and USD 975 million of notes due 2033, both senior unsecured and guaranteed by subsidiary guarantors. The proceeds redeemed USD 300 million of 2026 notes, and on 2025-08-12 an unsecured USD 1,000 million revolver was replaced by a five-year first-lien asset-based facility of up to USD 1,000 million with an uncommitted accordion of USD 500 million, undrawn at 2026-10-10. In the second quarter of 2026 the company repurchased USD 29 million of the 2028 notes and a nominal amount of the 2027 notes under a repurchase plan that has ended, and in the third quarter it moved USD 349 million of the 2027 notes to current liabilities.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for ADVANCE AUTO PARTS INC as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated credit view built from the financial foundation, the business and governance fact base and the seven supplied filings and earnings releases, through the quarter ended 2026-10-10.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-08-20_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the second quarter of 2026 | 2026-08-20 | 6fa6d0f76f705af9a8078a4e1b4a20159ae0682aa896d374dffc425d834ff4a2 | Issuer net leverage reconciliation at 2026-07-18. |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Advance Auto Parts is a recovering, thinly profitable retailer: USD 3,979 million of liquidity and no maturity before October 2027 protect creditors near term, but 6.67x leverage and supplier-finance reliance leave little room for another earnings setback.

Net debt is USD 303 million, or 0.60x, because cash of USD 3,085 million offsets most of the USD 3,388 million of debt; the pro forma figure after the dividend declared on 2026-10-26 is not established in the financial foundation. Reported EBITDA of USD 508 million covers cash interest of USD 200 million 2.54x. The main downside path is a withdrawal of the rating-linked supplier finance, USD 2,600 million, which would drain cash faster than debt service does. Covenant headroom, ratings and recovery are not established.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C07; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Key findings

Liquidity, not earnings, carries this credit through the next two maturities. Cash of USD 3,085 million plus USD 894 million of undrawn asset-based facility is USD 3,979 million, against the 2027 notes of USD 350 million and the 2028 notes of USD 300 million at year-end principal, so cash alone covers the 2027 notes 8.81x and both notes 4.75x. About USD 2,300 million of the cash sits in accounts under springing control that become restricted on a default or covenant breach, and the facility imposes minimum availability tests, so the usable amount is lower than the headline. The dividend declared on 2026-10-26 is a post-balance-sheet event whose pro forma effect on cash and net debt is not established in Financial foundation. Near-term refinancing risk is therefore low, and the test moves to the 2030 wall of USD 1,475 million.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 89–92

Leverage is high on reported EBITDA and the fixed-charge load is heavy. Total debt is 6.67x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and on the company's own adjusted EBITDAR, gross debt with lease liabilities is 4.82x. Cover is 2.54x on cash interest and 2.38x on accrued interest, and adjusted EBITDAR covers rent plus cash interest only 1.60x. The mechanism is that rent of USD 524 million and interest of USD 200 million come ahead of equity, so a fall in earnings reduces cover faster than the debt ratio suggests. In fiscal 2025, when EBITDA was USD 229 million, leverage was 14.90x, which shows how little earnings erosion the structure absorbs.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C14; calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 10

Cash generation has turned but depends on payables. Free cash flow was USD 109 million in the forty weeks to 2026-10-10 against USD -277 million a year earlier, yet the last twelve months convert only 17.32% of EBITDA into free cash flow of USD 88 million. Payables swung from a USD 270 million outflow to a USD 94 million inflow, and restructuring cash charges fell from USD 130 million to USD 19 million. The gains are therefore partly timing and one-off relief, and capital expenditure guided at about USD 300 million for fiscal 2026 will absorb a rising share of cash as restructuring costs fade.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10

Supplier finance is the largest swing factor in liquidity. Confirmed supplier finance obligations of USD 2,600 million are 84.83% of accounts payable, they sit outside debt, and the annual report links bank participation to the company's credit rating. A repeat of the fiscal 2025 payables outflow of USD 469 million would absorb 15.20% of cash, and a wider withdrawal would shorten payment terms across the inventory base. This is why a rating action matters more here than a maturity.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C17; 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 49, 103; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 14

Structure and governance leave noteholders behind a secured facility with no sponsor to lean on. The undrawn USD 1,000 million first-lien facility ranks ahead of the unsecured notes on receivables, inventory and cash, the guarantor list and credit agreements were not supplied, and the company is widely held with no controlling holder named. Governance risk is Medium on the assessment in Business & governance: the dividend was cut and no shares were bought back, but dividends continued while free cash flow was negative. The consequence is that creditor protection depends on documents and ratings that are not in the file.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 88–91

The operating base is stabilising rather than growing. Net sales fell 5.4% in fiscal 2025 on store closures and are flat for forty weeks of 2026, comparable store sales are up 0.8%, professional customers are about half of sales and no customer reaches 10%. Gross margin rose to 45.29% from 43.21% and reported EBITDA reached USD 406 million against USD 127 million, but guidance of about USD 8,500 million of net sales for fiscal 2026 implies a slightly lower figure than the fifty-three-week base of fiscal 2025. The credit therefore rests on margin and working-capital discipline rather than on volume.
Basis: calculation C18; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is that net debt is small and the company's own net leverage is 2.2x, down from 2.4x two quarters earlier, with free cash flow guidance raised to about USD 150 million and comparable sales turning positive in the last four weeks of the third quarter. If the recovery holds, reported EBITDA above the last-twelve-month USD 508 million would move leverage below 6.67x without any debt repayment. The case for more caution is that the cash reflects the Worldpac proceeds and the 2025 notes rather than operating cash generation, USD 2,300 million of it is under springing control, and USD 2,600 million of supplier finance is rating-linked. The view would improve with sustained earnings growth and a rating that supports the supplier programs; it would worsen if confirmed supplier finance obligations fall sharply, if cash is used for payouts or deals, or if availability under the facility shrinks toward its stated floors.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C06; calculation C09; calculation C10; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2, 10; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14
### Limitations

- No agency rating, market price or peer set was supplied, so the judgement that refinancing access is adequate rests on liquidity and fixed-rate maturities alone; a speculative-grade rating with a negative outlook would lower that judgement, and an upgrade would raise it.

- The executed facility agreement was not available, so usable liquidity is stated as cash plus availability without covenant headroom; a binding springing test would reduce the liquidity buffer judged here.

- Management guidance as of 2026-11-05 is unaudited and is the only forward evidence, so the outlook for 2026 earnings and free cash flow is as reliable as that guidance; a miss would reverse the view that cash generation has turned.
- The downside scenario is built from observed fiscal 2025 flows rather than a forecast, so it shows the order of magnitude of a payables shock and does not give a probability or a timetable.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest credit support is liquidity: USD 3,979 million of cash and availability against USD 650 million of notes due in 2027 and 2028 removes near-term refinancing pressure and gives time for the turnaround. A second support is the recovery in earnings and cash flow, with forty-week reported EBITDA of USD 406 million and free cash flow of USD 109 million, which if sustained lowers the leverage ratio without any repayment. A third is the breadth of the customer base, with half of sales to professional customers on short terms and no customer at 10%, which limits concentration risk. A fourth is the payout record since 2024, with the dividend cut by more than half and no share repurchases, which keeps cash in the business. A fifth is the maturity profile, which is entirely fixed-rate unsecured notes with no scheduled maturity until October 2027.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The most material weakness is leverage on thin earnings: total debt is 6.67x reported EBITDA and cover is 2.54x on cash interest, so there is little room for a setback. A second is the supplier-finance float of USD 2,600 million, which is rating-linked and would drain cash if withdrawn. A third is structural: a first-lien facility ranks ahead of the notes and USD 2,300 million of cash is under springing control. A fourth is the fixed claims outside debt, lease liabilities of USD 2,189 million and rent of USD 524 million, which leave EBITDAR cover of rent plus cash interest at 1.60x. A fifth is the shrinking sales base and unfinished restructuring, with net sales down 5.4% in fiscal 2025 and a further USD 5 million to USD 10 million of restructuring cost expected in fiscal 2026.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 19

### Company description

The company is a North American aftermarket auto parts retailer and distributor serving professional installers and do-it-yourself customers from company stores, independently owned Carquest stores and online, with net sales of USD 8,601 million in fiscal 2025 and nearly all of them in the United States. Demand is replacement-driven and recurring, which supports cash-flow visibility, but it is discretionary at the margin because elective maintenance can be deferred. Since 2024 the company sold Worldpac for net proceeds of USD 1,440 million, closed 10.90% of its stores and refinanced, so the creditor question is whether a smaller, simpler business can hold earnings while it carries USD 3,388 million of debt.
Basis: calculation C18; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 4–9, 105
### Ownership and group structure

The company is publicly listed with no sponsor or controlling holder named, and the proxy statement that would show large holders and related-party dealings was not supplied. The issuer is the parent and borrower, with subsidiaries that guarantee the notes and the facility, and the guarantor list was not supplied. Financial policy has been to cut the dividend, buy back no shares and keep the cash from the Worldpac sale and the 2025 notes, but dividends were paid while free cash flow was negative. The implication is that there is no sponsor extraction pathway but also no sponsor support, and policy risk sits with the board.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 37, 68
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue comes from many small repeat purchases at the point of need, with parts and batteries at 64% of sales and professional customers about half, so the base is granular and no customer reaches 10% of net sales. Volume depends on vehicles on the road, miles driven and weather, and the filing names fuel costs, inflation and tariffs as pressures on discretionary spending; price increases from suppliers have been partly passed through. Comparable store sales rose 0.8% in fiscal 2025 and in the forty weeks of 2026 but fell 1.2% in the third quarter before turning positive in its last four weeks. Revenue is therefore recurring and cyclical in a mild way rather than contracted, and it is not structurally declining apart from closures.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 40, 76, 105; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 20–22; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are largely fixed in the short run: rent is a fixed claim of USD 524 million over the last twelve months, about 80% of stores are leased and most employees work in stores, so volume declines cut margins quickly. Gross margin recovered to 45.29% for forty weeks of 2026 after lower-margin liquidation sales and charges in 2025, and selling and administrative costs excluding restructuring fell to 41.5% of sales in fiscal 2025 from 41.9%. Inventory is largely on last-in first-out accounting, with a reserve of USD 133 million at 2026-10-10 against USD 104 million at year end, so inflation reduces reported gross profit without a cash cost. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through store closures and hub conversion, but not against a sharp fall in volume.
Basis: calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 49; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital expenditure was USD 252 million in fiscal 2025 and is guided to about USD 300 million for fiscal 2026, and cash taxes paid were only USD 13 million in fiscal 2025, so the drain between EBITDA and free cash flow is capex, working capital, rent already inside EBITDA, interest and restructuring cash. Free cash flow was USD -298 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 109 million in the forty weeks to 2026-10-10, giving a last-twelve-month conversion of 17.32% of reported EBITDA. Capex can be flexed down in a downturn, but store and supply-chain investment is the main source of the recovery, so cutting it would slow the turnaround. Conversion is not yet durable enough to fund repayment of the 2030 wall from internal cash flow.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10
### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most: the company competes with national chains, independents, internet retailers and dealers on availability, price and service, and the filing warns that the company might not be able to pass higher supplier costs on to customers, so pricing power is limited and gross margin depends on mix and sourcing. Supplier power is the next, because the company buys from several hundred vendors and relies on favourable payment terms and supplier finance, which a downgrade could remove. In the analyst's judgement buyer power is moderate for professionals, who value same-day availability, and higher for do-it-yourself customers, who can switch easily. The threat of new entrants and substitutes is mainly online retail and changes in vehicle use, which are slow-moving credit risks rather than near-term ones.
### PEST analysis

Political and economic factors are material because tariffs led some suppliers to raise prices in fiscal 2025, although the company says the effect has not been material so far, a court decision in February 2026 opened a refund process that produced USD 26 million of benefit in the second quarter, and inflation and fuel costs affect miles driven and customer spending. Regulatory and technological factors, including emissions policy and vehicle electrification, are named in the annual report but are slow-moving and are not a primary credit driver on the provided materials. The credit consequence of the political and economic factors is margin volatility, which the company manages mainly through supplier price pass-through.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are liquidity of USD 3,979 million, a broad customer base, a recovery in earnings and a fixed-rate maturity profile starting in October 2027. Weaknesses are leverage of 6.67x, supplier-finance reliance of USD 2,600 million, fixed claims for leases and rent, and a shrinking sales base. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are further margin gains from the hub network and a rating that supports supplier programs, and the main threats are a withdrawal of supplier finance, a sustained fall in comparable sales and a use of cash for payouts.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C06; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

Supports are liquidity, a maturity profile without scheduled repayments before October 2027, positive free cash flow in 2026 and a payout policy that has kept cash in the business. Constraints are leverage of 6.67x, cover of 2.54x on cash interest, reliance on supplier finance, and structural priority held by the facility over receivables, inventory and cash. The trend is improving on earnings and cash flow and stable on liquidity, and the missing datapoints are the credit agreement terms, ratings and the proxy statement. The net result is a financial profile that is adequate for near-term obligations and weak for a stress case.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C06; calculation C07; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months, management guides to net sales of about USD 8,500 million, adjusted operating margin of 4.00% to 4.30%, capital expenditure of about USD 300 million and free cash flow of about USD 150 million for fiscal 2026, which implies flat sales and margin-led improvement. Tailwinds are lower restructuring cost, a store and hub programme, and tariff refunds; headwinds are cost inflation, softer do-it-yourself demand in summer, and the interest cost of the 2025 notes. Over three to five years the credit depends on whether the earnings recovery lets the company repay or refinance USD 1,475 million due in FY2030 and USD 1,325 million after it without using the cash cushion.
Basis: calculation C12; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_aap-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-10-10_aap-20261010.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 19
### Qualitative downside scenario

The initiating condition is a withdrawal by banks from the supplier finance programs, for example after a rating action, at a time when comparable sales are again negative. The first operational break is shorter payment terms on inventory, which in fiscal 2025 produced a USD 469 million payables outflow that contributed to operating cash flow of USD -46 million even without a bank withdrawal. The financial transmission is cash falling, free cash flow turning negative as capex of about USD 300 million continues, and EBITDA falling back to the fiscal 2025 level of USD 229 million, which would put total debt of USD 3,388 million at 14.79x and cover cash interest of USD 200 million only 1.15x. Cash and availability of USD 3,979 million would cover the 2027 and 2028 notes in that case, but they would not cover the 2030 wall, and restricted cash and availability floors would reduce usable liquidity. Management levers are cutting capex, slowing store openings and withholding dividends; the observable triggers are falling confirmed supplier finance, negative comparable sales and shrinking facility availability.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C18; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_aap-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 49, 67–68
### Overall credit view

Overall, Advance Auto Parts presents an adequate near-term business and liquidity profile supported by USD 3,979 million of liquidity, a maturity profile with no repayment before October 2027 and a recovery in earnings, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 6.67x, reliance on supplier finance, structural priority held by a secured facility and heavy fixed claims. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but still working-capital dependent. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on sustained earnings, the supplier-finance programs and market access that cannot be assessed without ratings. The primary downside path is a withdrawal of supplier finance combined with weaker sales. Further analysis would require the credit documents, ratings, the proxy statement and the guarantor list. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: loss of rating-linked supplier finance.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C10; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
